newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: China slams Guatemala for its "erroneous position".
newsitem.headline: China slams Guatemala for its "erroneous position".

text.p: China told the Security Council on Friday it vetoed a resolution to send U.N. peacekeepers to Guatemala because of that country's "erroneous position" in supporting Taiwan.
But its U.N. ambassador, Qin Huasun, added that China might reconsider if Guatemala "moves to remove the obstacles."

"We welcome and are gratified with the peace agreement reached by the two parties in Guatemala and sincerely hope that peace and stability will prevail in the country," he said, referring to an accord signed December 29 that ended 30 years of civil war.

"Regrettably, however, the government of Guatemala has, for four consecutive years, unscrupulously supported activities aimed at splitting China in the U.N. in flagrant violation of the purposes and principles of the U.N. Charter in disregard of repeated demarches of the Chinese government."

"Furthermore, it was bent on inviting, in disregard of solemn warnings...the Taiwan authorities to the signing ceremony of the peace agreement in Guatemala, thereby providing them with a venue for secessionist activities against China," Qin said.

China, which took over the U.N. seat held by Taiwan in 1971, regards the Asian economic powerhouse as a renegade province. For the past four years Beijing has successfully repulsed a bid by a number of small countries to obtain U.N. membership for Taiwan.
Qin said the Guatemalan authorities could not expect to have China's cooperation in the Security Council "while taking actions to infringe upon China's sovereignty and territorial integrity."
"No country's peace process should be at the expense of another country's sovereignty and territorial integrity," he said.
Qin said China had made "reasonable suggestions" aimed at resolving the issue but Guatemala had "turned a deaf ear...and clung to its erroneous position."

But if Guatemala was "indeed sincere, treasurers its peace process and moves to remove the obstacles, the Chinese delegation may reconsider the authorization of the deployment of military observers in Guatemala by the Security Council," Qin said.
